lines.japanese: 渡来さんたちと別れてから、携帯を開いて時間を確かめてみた。
lines.english: After parting from Watarai and the others, I flipped open my phone to check the time.

lines.japanese: まだ２０時になってない……帰り道の途中でゲームショップへ寄っても、まだ間に合う時間だ。
lines.english: It was not yet eight. There was still time to stop by the game shop on the way home.

lines.japanese: うーん、それなら新作ゲームの確認でもしに行こうかな。今月は購入を控えたいところだけど、見にいくだけならいいはずだ。うん、そうしよう。
lines.english: In that case, perhaps I would go see what new games had come in. I meant to keep my spending down this month, but merely looking could do no harm. Yes. I would do that.

lines.japanese: お店に行くならここを通りぬけた方が早い。僕は生ゴミの臭いに鼻をつまみつつ、路地裏に足を踏みいれた。
lines.english: The quickest way to the shop led through here. Pinching my nose against the reek of garbage, I stepped into the alley.

lines.japanese: ちょっと薄暗い場所ではあるけど、何度か通ったことのある道だ。僕は急ぎ足で通路の向こう側へ向かう。
lines.english: It was a little dark, but I had used this route several times before. I quickened my pace toward the opening at the far end.

lines.japanese: 「グァウッ！」
lines.english: “Grr-woof!”
“What...?”

lines.japanese: 突然の唸り声に、一瞬なにが現れたのか反応できなかった。ワンテンポ遅れて顔を向けると、野良犬が後ろ足を蹴りながら僕のことを睨んでいる。
lines.english: The sudden growl caught me so completely off guard that, for an instant, I could not even tell what had appeared. A beat later I turned. A stray dog was scraping its hind paws against the ground and glaring at me.

lines.japanese: 「わあっ！」
lines.english: “Whoa!”

lines.japanese: 僕は彼の縄張りに無断で踏みこんでしまったみたいだ。自分の領域を汚された彼は、鼻息も荒く侵入者を牽制した。
lines.english: It seemed I had trespassed upon his territory. His domain defiled, he snorted fiercely at the intruder in warning.

lines.japanese: 「ま、待ってよ、おれはちょっとここを通りたかっただけで……君と争う気なんてないんだ」
lines.english: “W-wait. I only wanted to pass through here... I don’t want to fight you.”

lines.japanese: 後ろに退がっても前に進んでも飛び掛られそうな剣幕だったから、僕は両手を伸ばして和平の交渉を申しでた。グレタガルドなら戦えるけど、ここは現実世界なんだ。
lines.english: He looked ready to spring whether I advanced or retreated, so I held out both hands and opened peace negotiations. I could fight in Gretagard, but this was the real world.

lines.japanese: そう、いくら人目がないからといって、こんなところで暴れるわけにはいかない。本気を出せば倒せるけど、牽制されたくらいで命をとるのは忍びない。
lines.english: Yes—even with no one watching, I could hardly cut loose in a place like this. At full strength I could defeat him, but taking a life over a warning would be too cruel.

lines.japanese: 「うん……やっぱり、ちゃんとした道を通って行くからさ。引きかえしてもいいかな」
lines.english: “All right... I’ll use a proper street after all. May I turn around?”

lines.japanese: 「ウゥゥゥ……」
lines.english: “Grrrr...”

lines.japanese: 彼はじりじりと僕との距離を測っていた。僕は伸ばした両手で、彼を押さえつけるようにしながら、一歩だけ後ろに退がる。なんでか分からないけど表情筋が引きつって、顔が勝手に笑っていた。
lines.english: He edged about, gauging the distance between us. I held both hands out as though pressing him back and took a single step in retreat. For some reason the muscles in my face had gone rigid, twisting it into a smile all by itself.

lines.japanese: 「グァウッ！」
lines.english: “Grr-woof!”

lines.japanese: 次の瞬間犬が飛びついてきて、僕の手首は鋭い牙に挟まれていた。腕から激痛が上ってくる。
lines.english: The next instant the dog launched himself at me, and sharp fangs closed around my wrist. Agony shot up my arm.

lines.japanese: 「うわあああっ！」
lines.english: “Aaaaaah!”

lines.japanese: 尻餅をついた僕はなんとか引きはがそうとぶんぶんと腕をふった。這いつくばったまま、僕はずるずると路地裏の出口へと向かう。
lines.english: I landed hard on my backside and flung my arm about, desperate to shake him loose. Still sprawled on the ground, I dragged myself inch by inch toward the mouth of the alley.

lines.japanese: 「ち、違うよ、おれはそんなつもりじゃ……あつッ！」
lines.english: “N-no, you’ve got it wrong. I didn’t mean to—ow!”

lines.japanese: もう片方の手で彼の頭を押さえながら体を引きずっていくと、外の光の届く位置で彼は僕を解放した。おそらく縄張りから出たんだろう。
lines.english: Holding his head off with my free hand, I hauled myself toward the light. Once we reached it, he released me. I had probably crossed out of his territory.

lines.japanese: 「ごめんね……勝手に通ろうとしたりして」
lines.english: “I’m sorry... for trying to cut through without permission.”

lines.japanese: 「アガルルル……」
lines.english: “Grrrrr...”

lines.japanese: 僕はまだ身構えている彼に頭を下げると、すぐにその場から離れてショッピング街へと戻った。
lines.english: I bowed to him while he remained braced for another attack, then hurried away and returned to the shopping district.

lines.japanese: 手から血を滴らせている僕を見て、道行くひとたちが顔をしかめていた。すぐに薬局に入って、消毒薬と包帯を買って手当てをしておいた。幸い、傷はそこまで深くはない。
lines.english: Passersby grimaced when they saw the blood dripping from my hand. I went straight into a drugstore, bought disinfectant and a bandage, and tended the wound. Fortunately, it was not too deep.

lines.japanese: 僕は薬局を出たあと、もう一度路地裏の入り口に立って頭を下げた。
lines.english: After leaving the drugstore, I went back to the entrance of the alley and bowed once more.

lines.japanese: 世界が平和でありますように。
lines.english: *May peace prevail on Earth*.

lines.japanese: 「なんだその怪我」
lines.english: “What happened to your hand?”

lines.japanese: 「あっ、針生さん」
lines.english: “Oh, Hariu.”

lines.japanese: 痛みがずきずきと疼きはじめたころ、通りがかった同級生に声をかけられた。こういうときは誰か話す相手がいれば、少しは痛みを紛らわせることが出来る。
lines.english: By the time the pain began to throb, a passing classmate called out to me. At least having someone to talk to might take my mind off it.

lines.japanese: 「ちょっと、野良犬に噛まれちゃって……はは」
lines.english: “A stray dog bit me... Ha ha.”

lines.japanese: 「はン、おまえもかよ」
lines.english: “Hah. You too?”

lines.japanese: 針生さんは口端だけつり上げて軽い笑みを浮かべると、しばらくそのまま、何か思いだすように体を揺らしていた。
lines.english: Hariu lifted one corner of his mouth in a faint smile. He stayed that way for a while, rocking slightly as though reliving some memory.

lines.japanese: 「そんでどうしたの。打ちのめしたわけ？」
lines.english: “So what’d you do? Beat the hell out of it?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、ま、まさか！　ちゃんと謝ってきましたよ」
lines.english: “What? N-no, of course not! I apologized properly.”

lines.japanese: 「謝る？　犬に？　意味わかんねえな、なんだおまえ、攻撃されたら謝ンのか」
lines.english: “Apologized? To a dog? What the hell does that mean? Something attacks you and you apologize?”

lines.japanese: 「違いますよ、おれが彼の領域に足を踏み入れたんです」
lines.english: “That’s different. I was the one who entered his territory.”

lines.japanese: 「ハッ」
lines.english: “Ha!”

lines.japanese: 針生さんは体を前屈みにして吐きだすように声を出した。開いた唇から、少しだけ白い歯が見えた。
lines.english: Hariu bent forward and spat the sound out. A sliver of white teeth showed through his parted lips.

lines.japanese: 「そういえば、離島には行かなかったんですか？」
lines.english: “Come to think of it, didn’t you go to the island?”

lines.japanese: 「ンー？　あァ、それなァ、野鳥だろ。もう究めた。いま新しい知識を探してンだよ」
lines.english: “Hm? Oh, that. The wild birds? Already mastered them. Now I’m looking for new knowledge.”

lines.japanese: 「まァ、目の前に面白いものがあるっちゃあんだけど、煮詰まンのにもうちょっと時間かかりそうだし……ンン、なんかもっとこう、ソッコー興味そそられるようなモンはねえかなあ」
lines.english: “Well, there’s something interesting right in front of me, but it’ll take a little longer to come together... Mm. Isn’t there anything that’ll grab me right this second?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そうですね……」
lines.english: “I see...”

lines.japanese: とは言っても、僕の趣味なんてごく一般的なゲームくらいだし、針生さんの期待に応えるのは難しいな。
lines.english: But my only hobby was perfectly ordinary: games. I doubted I had anything that could satisfy Hariu.

lines.japanese: 「だったら、おれ今からゲーム屋に行くんですけど、とりあえず一緒にどうですか」
lines.english: “Well, I’m going to a game shop now. Would you like to come along, for a start?”

lines.japanese: 「ゲームか……」
lines.english: “Games...”

lines.japanese: 針生さんの右眉がぴくりと上がる。ふらりと揺れていた頭の動きが、体の中心でぴたりと止まった。
lines.english: Hariu’s right eyebrow twitched. His head, which had been swaying loosely, stopped dead above the center of his body.

lines.japanese: 「おまえ、詳しいの」
lines.english: “You know much about games?”

lines.japanese: 「え、いや、詳しいってほどじゃないですよ。月に１本くらい新しいソフトを買ってるだけです。おれより詳しいひとなんていっぱいいますよ」
lines.english: “N-no, I wouldn’t say that. I only buy about one new title a month. There are plenty of people who know far more than I do.”

lines.japanese: 「へえ、どんなゲームやんの」
lines.english: “What kind do you play?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、興味あるんですか。それなら、うーん……スポーツものとかいいんじゃないかなあ。あとはＲＰＧなんて人気ありますよ。このまえ渡来さんも探してたみたいだし……」
lines.english: “Oh, are you interested? Then... perhaps a sports game would be good. RPGs are popular too. Watarai seemed to be looking for one the other day...”

lines.japanese: 「なんだ、その程度か」
lines.english: “That’s it?”

lines.japanese: 針生さんは鞄の中からペットボトルを取りだした。いつも口にしてるミネラルウォーターだ。
lines.english: Hariu pulled a plastic bottle from his bag—the mineral water he was always drinking.

lines.japanese: 「あ、いえ、これはあくまで初心者向けっていうか、ゲームの中でも浅い部分ですよ。もっと奥深いのもあるんですから」
lines.english: “No, those are only recommendations for beginners—the shallows of gaming, you might say. There are much deeper games than that.”

lines.japanese: 「はッ！　浅い部分ねえ……そんなに鼻息乱すなよ」
lines.english: “Ha! The shallows, huh? Don’t get yourself so worked up.”

lines.japanese: 「いまおまえが並べたゲームくらいならとっくにやり込んでんだ。もっとコアなゲームねえかなァ、まだ俺の脳味噌に入ってないようなやつ」
lines.english: “I’ve played everything you just named to death. Got anything more hardcore? Something that hasn’t made it into my brain yet?”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、シミュレーションゲームなんかどうですか。『信長の野心』なんて名作中の名作ですよ」
lines.english: “Then how about a simulation game? *Nobunaga’s Ambitions* is one of the all-time greats.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、あんなの俺でも作れンだろ。興味ねえな」
lines.english: “Hell, even I could make that. Doesn’t interest me.”

lines.japanese: 「面白いのに」
lines.english: “But it’s good.”

lines.japanese: 「この世界につまんねえモノなんかねえよ。楽しもうと思えば道端の犬のクソだって楽しめる。でも他にもっと笑えるもんが転がってるから、優先順位が低くなるだけの話」
lines.english: “Nothing in this world is boring. If you mean to enjoy it, you can enjoy dog shit by the roadside. It only ranks low because more interesting things are lying around. That’s all.”

lines.japanese: なんだかよく分からないけど、僕の好きなゲームが犬の糞と同列に語られてしまった。
lines.english: I was not entirely sure what he meant, but somehow a game I loved had been placed on the same level as dog excrement.

lines.japanese: 「もっとさあ、ニューエイジでハードコアなゲームはねえの」
lines.english: “C’mon, isn’t there anything more new-age and hardcore?”

lines.japanese: ニューエイジ……ってなんだろう。僕の知っている範囲だと、残りはギャルゲーくらいだ。でも一年生のころ、森里君にその話はしない方がいいと言われたことがある。
lines.english: New-age... What did that mean? The only field left within my knowledge was games about pretty girls. But during our first year, Morisato had told me not to talk about those with other people.

lines.japanese: 「俺ァ、もっとロックなゲームがやりたいんだ」
lines.english: “I want something more rock.”

lines.japanese: 「ロックって音楽ですよね？　音楽のゲームってことですか？」
lines.english: “Rock means music, doesn’t it? Do you mean a music game?”

lines.japanese: 「違う、もっと心が燃えるやつだよ」
lines.english: “No. Something that gets my heart pounding.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、萌えるやつですか」
lines.english: “Oh, something that gets your heart pounding?”

lines.japanese: なんだ、それなら僕の得意分野じゃないか。元々ギャルゲーを知ってるひとなら森里君もとめたりしないだろう。
lines.english: Oh. Then this was my specialty. If Hariu already knew about games built around pretty girls, surely Morisato would not object to my discussing them with him.

lines.japanese: 「あの、これなんてどうですか。ハマるとすごく面白いですよ」
lines.english: “Then how about this one? Once you get into it, it’s incredibly good.”

lines.japanese: 僕は鞄の中に入れていた家庭用ゲームを取りだした。
lines.english: I took a console game out of my bag.

lines.japanese: 「シャッ、フル、オンザステージ？　ふン、なんだこりゃ」
lines.english: “Shuf... fle... On the Stage? Hmph. What the hell is this?”

lines.japanese: 「知りませんか、これすごく萌えますよ」
lines.english: “You don’t know it? This one will really get your heart pounding.”

lines.japanese: 「へえ、そんなに燃えんの。どんなジャンルだ、これ」
lines.english: “Yeah? Gets your heart pounding that much? What genre is it?”

lines.japanese: 「恋愛ゲームです」
lines.english: “It’s a romance game.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、恋愛シミュレーションってやつか。それなら十年前に卒業した」
lines.english: “Oh, one of those dating simulations. I graduated from those ten years ago.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、いまはアドベンチャーの方が主流ですよ」
lines.english: “Adventure games are more common now.”

lines.japanese: 「へえ、そうなの」
lines.english: “Are they?”

lines.japanese: 「はい。もう何年かまえに、ビジュアルノベルっていうジャンルが出始めてから、ギャルゲー界は一変したんです。覚えておいた方がいいですよ」
lines.english: “Yes. Several years ago, the rise of the visual novel transformed the entire market for games built around pretty girls. You should remember that.”

lines.japanese: 「フゥーン……」
針生さんはパッケージの表と裏をひらひらと返しながら絵柄を見つめた。少しは興味を持ってくれただろうか。
lines.english: Hariu fluttered the package back and forth, studying the artwork on its front and rear. Had I managed to interest him at least a little?

lines.japanese: 「第一印象ではどのキャラが気に入りそうですか？」
lines.english: “Which character catches your eye at first glance?”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　どのキャラっておまえ、こいつらみんな同じような顔じゃねえか」
lines.english: “Which character? They all have the same damn face.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そうか……萌え絵に疎いひとはこっち系のキャラを“アニメ的な絵”で一括りにしがちですね」
lines.english: “Oh, I see... People unfamiliar with cute-girl art do tend to lump all these characters together as ‘anime drawings.’”

lines.japanese: 「ン？　ああ、なんだ、萌えってそっちの話か」
lines.english: “Hm? Oh. So that’s what you meant by ‘heart-pounding.’”

lines.japanese: えっ、なんのことだろう？　萌えに他の意味なんてあるのかな。
lines.english: What did he mean by *that*? Could “heart-pounding” mean something else?

lines.japanese: 「どうだろうな……ネットでよく聞く萌えという概念が、いまひとつ俺には理解できないんだ」
lines.english: “Hard to say... I’ve never quite understood what people online see in this whole cute-girl thing.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、分からないんですか？　うーん、それは勿体ないなあ。すごくいいものですよ、お勧めできるものならいっぱいあるんです」
lines.english: “You don’t understand it? What a waste. It’s a wonderful thing. I could recommend any number of games.”

lines.japanese: 「これはやってみないと分かりませんから、ハードがあるなら一度試してみたらどうですか？」
lines.english: “You really have to play one to understand. If you have the console, why not give this a try?”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ聞くけど、このギャルゲーってやつは大仏やダムより面白いの」
lines.english: “Then let me ask you: are these pretty-girl games more interesting than a Great Buddha or a dam?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、それは……どうでしょう。おれはそう思いますけど」
lines.english: “Well... I’m not sure. I think it is, but...”

lines.japanese: 「ふぅん。まあいいや、返す」
lines.english: “Hmm. Whatever. Here.”

lines.japanese: 僕が悩んでいたら、ゲームを返されてしまった。残念だけど、そんなには気に入ってもらえなかったみたいだ。
lines.english: While I struggled to answer, he handed the game back. Regrettably, it did not seem to have won him over.

lines.japanese: だけどゲームすべてに興味がないって感じじゃなさそうだ。
lines.english: Still, he did not seem wholly uninterested in games themselves.

lines.japanese: 「そうだ、今からゲームショップに行くんですよ。一緒に行きませんか？」
lines.english: “That’s right—I’m headed to a game shop now. Would you like to come?”

lines.japanese: 「ああいや、今日はいい。そのうち興味が沸いたら、こっちで調べて勝手にやるし」
lines.english: “Nah, not today. If I get interested, I’ll look into it myself and play whatever I please.”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、そうですか……お勧めがあるんだけどなあ……」
lines.english: “I see... But I have so many recommendations...”

lines.japanese: 「そういやおまえ、さっき明日香にも勧めたって言ってたなァ。もしかして、あいつにもこのゲーム勧めたの」
lines.english: “Speaking of which, you said you recommended something to Asuka. Don’t tell me you recommended this to her.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、だって、これは女の子と付き合うゲームですよ。渡来さんは女の子だから、興味がないんじゃないかな」
lines.english: “Of course not. This is a game about dating girls. Watarai is a girl herself, so I doubt she would be interested.”

lines.japanese: 「そりゃそうだ。あいつ萌えとか全く理解できなそうだし、だいたい本人からしてまったく萌えねえもんな」
lines.english: “No kidding. She’d never understand the appeal in the first place, and the girl herself hasn’t got an ounce of it.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、そ、そうですか？　渡来さんなんて、クラスにファンも多いみたいだし……その、プリンセスとかって」
lines.english: “R-really? Watarai seems to have plenty of admirers in class... They even call her the princess.”

lines.japanese: 「げらげらげら。あいつはお姫様ってタイプじゃないだろ、萌えの欠片もねえよ」
lines.english: “Gahahahaha! She’s hardly the princess type. There isn’t a shred of cute-girl appeal in her.”

lines.japanese: 「そうかなあ、渡来さんなんてゲームのヒロインになってもおかしくないのに」
lines.english: “I don’t know. Watarai could easily be the heroine of a game.”

lines.japanese: やっぱり針生さんは萌えの概念が分かってないんだ。可哀想に。
lines.english: Hariu truly did not understand what made a girl appealing. Poor man.

lines.japanese: 「俺なら買わねえなあ、そんなギャルゲー。タダでもいらねえよ。そんで、あいつはどんなゲーム買ったの」
lines.english: “I wouldn’t buy a pretty-girl game with her in it. Wouldn’t take it for free. So what game did she buy?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、それが、渡来さんがなんのゲームを買ったのか、おれも教えてもらえなくて」
lines.english: “That’s the thing. Watarai wouldn’t tell me what she bought.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだか見られるのが恥ずかしかったみたいなんです。中古のＲＰＧを見てたのは分かるんだけどなあ」
lines.english: “She seemed embarrassed to let me see it. I do know she was looking at used RPGs...”

lines.japanese: 「明日香がＲＰＧ？　はあ、今度はなに企んでんだかあいつ──」
lines.english: “Asuka, playing an RPG? Hah. What’s she plotting this time—”

lines.japanese: 「──ンン？　ちょっと待て、明日香は中古のＲＰＧって言ったのか」
lines.english: “—Mm? Wait. You said Asuka was looking at a used RPG?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、はい。そうですけど……」
lines.english: “Yes. Why?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ……ああ、そういうことかァ。ククッ、クックック、あいつ、相変わらず面白いことへの嗅覚が優れてンだなァ」
lines.english: “Ah... Ah, so that’s it. Heh. Hehehe. Her nose for amusement is as keen as ever.”

lines.japanese: どうしたんだろう、針生さんは面白そうにくすくす笑いはじめた。
lines.english: What had come over him? Hariu began to chuckle in obvious delight.

lines.japanese: 「ハッ、ハハッ、ハッハッハ……そうか、そいつァ面白えな。なあ委員長。おまえもまんざら捨てたモンじゃなかったんだな」
lines.english: “Ha! Hahaha... I see. Now that’s funny. Hey, class rep. Perhaps you aren’t entirely hopeless after all.”

lines.japanese: 「どういうことですか？」
lines.english: “What do you mean?”

lines.japanese: 「おまえが面白いやつってことだ」
lines.english: “I mean you’re an amusing guy.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、ありがとう……ございます？」
lines.english: “Thank you... I think?”

lines.japanese: なんでかは分からないけど、針生さんに気に入ってもらえたみたいだ。もし製作のことをお願いするなら、今がいいのかもしれない。
lines.english: I did not know why, but I seemed to have won Hariu’s favor. If I meant to ask him about the anthology, this might be my chance.

lines.japanese: 「あ、あの、もしいま言ったことが本当なら、月曜日から一緒に卒業文集の製作をやりませんか」
lines.english: “If you really mean that, would you work on the graduation anthology with us starting Monday?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、例の活動か。そうなァ、面白くできそうなァ。じゃあ、他に楽しいモン見つかんなかったら手伝うよ」
lines.english: “Oh, that project. Hmm. Might be possible to make it interesting. If I don’t find anything more fun, I’ll help.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ！」
lines.english: “What?!”

lines.japanese: 大きな声を出してしまった。自分でお願いしておいてなんだけど、いまの嘘みたいな返事が、一瞬信じられなかった。
lines.english: My voice came out far too loud. I had made the request myself, yet his answer sounded so impossible that for an instant I could not believe I had heard it.

lines.japanese: 「針生さん！　ありがとうございます！」
lines.english: “Hariu! Thank you!”

lines.japanese: 「まァ、そんな熱心には入れこまねえと思うけど」
lines.english: “Don’t expect me to throw myself into it or anything.”

lines.japanese: 「それでいいです！　よろしくお願いします！」
lines.english: “That’s perfectly fine! Thank you!”

lines.japanese: 僕は何度も頭を下げた。これでようやく僕の班が全員揃うんだ。
lines.english: I bowed again and again. At last, my group would have all its members.

lines.japanese: 頭を上げると、針生さんはペットボトルのキャップを外して、ミネラルウォーターを喉に流しこんでいた。ごっごっという音が聞こえてくる。
lines.english: When I raised my head, Hariu had unscrewed the cap and was pouring mineral water down his throat. I could hear it glugging.

lines.japanese: 彼はふうと息をつくと、キャップを閉めながら僕に視線を合わせた。
lines.english: He let out a breath, screwed the cap back on, and met my eyes.

lines.japanese: 「さて、おまえも用事があるなら早く行けよ。俺は帰る」
lines.english: “All right. If you’ve got somewhere to be, get going. I’m heading home.”

lines.japanese: 「あの、やっぱり一緒にゲームを見には行きませんか？」
lines.english: “Are you sure you won’t come look at games with me?”

lines.japanese: 「やめとくって言ったでしょう。趣味のことならひとりで楽しみなよ委員長」
lines.english: “I told you I’m not going. Enjoy your hobbies by yourself, class rep.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんと一緒に行きたかったけど、仕方ない、今度また誘ってみよう。
lines.english: I had wanted to go with Hariu, but there was nothing for it. I would invite him again another time.

lines.japanese: 「……なあ、おい」
lines.english: “...Hey. Hold up.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: ゲームショップに向かおうと振り向きかけたとき、針生さんから声がかかった。あれ、なんだろう。
lines.english: I had just begun to turn toward the game shop when Hariu called me back. What could he want?

lines.japanese: 「おまえ、ウイングクエストって知ってるか」
lines.english: “You ever heard of Wing Quest?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？　なんですか、それ」
lines.english: “What is that?”

lines.japanese: 「だよなあ」
lines.english: “Thought not.”

lines.japanese: くっくっと笑い声が聞こえたかと思うと、針生さんは僕の質問には答えずに、そのまま去ってしまった。
lines.english: I heard a low chuckle, and then Hariu walked away without answering my question.

lines.japanese: ウイングクエスト……有名なゲームのタイトルだけど、何故だろう。内容は思い出せないけど、どこか懐かしい感じがした。
lines.english: Wing Quest... It was the title of a famous game. I could remember nothing about it, yet for some reason it felt strangely nostalgic.

lines.japanese: 「気のせいかなあ……」
lines.english: “Maybe I’m imagining it...”

lines.japanese: そうだ、針生さんも、知っているゲームのことを聞いてみただけで、別に深い意味なんてなかったんだ。
lines.english: Of course. Hariu had only asked whether I knew a game he happened to know. It did not have to mean anything deeper.

lines.japanese: それよりも、月曜日からはみんなで活動ができる。そのことが嬉しくて、僕はゲームショップまで駆け足で向かった。
lines.english: More importantly, the whole group could begin working together on Monday. Delighted by the thought, I hurried to the game shop.

lines.japanese: 電車に揺られて駅から歩いてくる途中、雲の流れる冬の夜空を眺めていた。
lines.english: After the train ride home, I watched clouds drift across the winter night as I walked from the station.

lines.japanese: そういえば夜空を眺めた記憶ってあんまりないなあ。どうしてだろう。僕の記憶にあるのは、いつも冬の夜空ばかりだ。
lines.english: Come to think of it, I had very few memories of gazing at the night sky. Why was that? The skies I did remember were always winter skies.

lines.japanese: いつの時代か、ギリシアの天文学者が夜空に見とれて穴に落っこちたらしい。この高い空を見ていると、その気持ちが分かる気がする。
lines.english: They say that, once, a Greek astronomer became so absorbed in the heavens that he fell into a hole. Looking up at that immense sky, I felt I understood him.

lines.japanese: 上ばかり見ていたら羽田家の屋根が見えてきた。そうだ、家に着く前に教えてもらった森里君の電話番号にかけてみよう。
lines.english: As I kept looking upward, the roof of the Haneda house came into view. Before I went inside, I would try the number I had been given for Morisato.

lines.japanese: 僕は携帯を取りだすと、メモリ番号「０２」を呼び出して通話ボタンを押してみた。
lines.english: I took out my phone, called up memory slot 02, and pressed the call button.

lines.japanese: 押してはみたものの、なにを話したらいいんだろう。でも森里君が喜んでくれるといいな。
lines.english: Now that I had called, what was I supposed to say? Still, I hoped Morisato would be glad to hear from me.

lines.japanese: ぷっぷっぷっ
lines.english: Beep, beep, beep.

lines.japanese: そうだ、僕のクラスのことでも話してみようかな。渡来さんのこと、山科さんのこと、それと針生さんのこと。渡来さんや山科さんは森里君も同じクラスだったから、覚えてるかもしれない。
lines.english: Perhaps I could tell him about my class—about Watarai, Yamashina, and Hariu. Morisato had once been in the same class as Watarai and Yamashina, so he might remember them.

lines.japanese: ぷっ
lines.english: Beep.

lines.japanese: 「留守番電話にお繋ぎします」
lines.english: “Connecting you to voicemail.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: だけど、携帯から聞こえてきた声は、僕が想像していた笑い声ではなく、機械的な女性の声だった。続いて、留守番電話のメッセージの説明に入る。
lines.english: But the voice from the phone was not the laughter I had imagined. It was an automated female voice, which went on to explain how to leave a message.

lines.japanese: 「おかけになったお客様は、電波の届かない場所におられるか、電源が入っておりません。ピーという発信音のあとに……」
lines.english: “The person you are calling is either outside the service area or has their phone switched off. Please leave your message after the tone...”

lines.japanese: 僕はその説明の途中で電話を切った。普通に話すのも難しいのに、留守番電話にメッセージを入れるなんて難易度の高い真似が出来るわけがない。
lines.english: I hung up before the explanation had finished. Ordinary conversation was difficult enough. There was no possibility I could manage the advanced feat of leaving a recorded message.

lines.japanese: そのあと何度か試してみたけど、森里君の携帯に電波が繋がることはなかった。仕方ない、手もかじかんできたし家に入ろう。
lines.english: I tried several more times afterward, but Morisato’s phone never connected. There was nothing for it. My hands were going numb, so I went inside.

lines.japanese: 「ただいま」
lines.english: “I’m home.”

lines.japanese: 居間に入ると食事が用意されていた。しまった、また小鳩を待たせちゃった。
lines.english: Dinner was waiting in the living room. Oh no—I had kept Kobato waiting again.

lines.japanese: 彼女は部屋にいるみたいだ。訊ねて謝ろうかとも思ったけど、せっかくの金曜日に友達と電話でもしてたら悪いし、一人で食事を済ませて食器も洗っておいた。
lines.english: She seemed to be in her room. I considered going to apologize, but it would be rude to interrupt if she was spending her Friday night talking to a friend. I ate alone and washed the dishes afterward.

lines.japanese: きっと、小鳩にも友達と話が止まらない日があるに違いない。僕にだって、明日の予定が出来たくらいなんだ。
lines.english: Surely even Kobato had nights when she and her friends could talk forever. After all, even I had managed to make plans for tomorrow.

lines.japanese: 部屋に戻ってから渡来さんに描いてもらった地図を見ながら、何度もパソコンで行き方を確かめた。
lines.english: Back in my room, I studied the map Watarai had drawn and checked the route on my computer again and again.

lines.japanese: ２２時を過ぎるとそれにも疲れたから、寝坊しないように早く寝ることにした。明日は作業が進みますように。
lines.english: After ten, even that wore me out. I decided to go to bed early so I would not oversleep. May tomorrow’s work go well.

lines.japanese: おやすみなさい。
lines.english: Good night.
